A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same three probing experiments, datasets, and seven-model study despite the changed title and extensive rewriting. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Fig-QA spatial-analysis and multiple-choice results, plus MUNCH lexical-substitution and syntactic-perturbation experiments, including model-specific appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds literal-anchor diagnostics, permutation-test findings, and a 50-item human evaluation in Section 5.1 and Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The reported geometric computation changes locally: v1 describes SVD on stacked sentence embeddings and a truncated reconstruction, whereas v2 specifies centered affine-plane direction vectors and orthonormal singular-vector bases (Section 4.3). The three probing procedures otherwise remain intact. This establishes a revision to the stated computation, not that the experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use Fig-QA and MUNCH with the same interpretation, substitution, genre, novelty, and syntactic-perturbation coverage. The new human evaluation assesses existing o3-mini interpretations; it introduces no additional dataset, language, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: The matched experiments retain DeepSeek-V3, Qwen-Turbo, GPT-4, GPT-4o, o3-mini, DeepSeek-R1, and LLaMA-3.1-8B. LMA becomes LLaMA in labels. Multiple-choice and similarity-based comparisons already appear in v1; their greater prominence in v2 does not introduce new comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds a targeted validation protocol: one annotator scores 25 o3-mini outputs from each of the bottom-200 and top-200 dp regions using a 0–2 rubric. Figure 7 also revises the documented contextual prompts from tagged target words to a # placeholder plus the original word. The main benchmark settings remain unchanged; rerunning them is not established.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands validation of the geometric probe beyond v1's correlations and illustrative cases. Section 5.1 adds permutation controls, Appendix F checks the generated literal anchor's similarity and balance against human references, and Appendix G tests geometric separation against human judgments. These address the validity of the central measurement.

E5.justification: V1 reports means, standard deviations, and correlation coefficients without inferential uncertainty. V2 adds correlation permutation tests and, for the human evaluation, a bootstrap 95% confidence interval of [0.76, 1.44] for the mean-score difference and a Mann–Whitney test with p approximately 1.05e-6. These are substantive additions to statistical assessment, not evidence of additional generation runs.

E6.justification: The main benchmark tables retain their numerical results, but v2 withdraws the headline 15–25% conceptual-irrelevance figure and adds substantive validation findings: human scores of 1.96 versus 0.84, anchor-similarity distributions, and near-zero permuted correlations. Figure 5 also changes the reported comparison, although its R1 'full dataset' values match the news-only distribution in Figure 14 rather than the full-data distribution in Figure 12.

T1.justification: Sections 3.1 and 4.3 explicitly formulate the reference region as an affine plane and replace v1's truncated-reconstruction account with centered direction vectors and orthonormal bases. V1's Equation 2 is removed. This is a localized mathematical correction/refinement; neither version presents a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion shift from claims about conceptual-error prevalence and an inherent metaphor-literal repository to narrower behavioral diagnostics. V2 removes the 15–25% error claim and the 'first' investigation claim, and replaces asserted context neglect with persistent lexical associations that may help familiar metaphors while biasing novel ones.

C2.justification: V2 treats geometry as a relative, embedding-dependent proxy and explicitly states that lexical overlap does not establish ignored context. It softens claims about LLaMA's understanding and treats random shuffle as an artificial stress test. The limitations now address reference-plane construction, embedding dependence, and restricted generalization from single-word metaphors. Genre differences are reinterpreted through conventionalization and contextual dependence rather than chiefly training-data differences.

D1.justification: V2 adds dataset licenses, more explicit geometric-computation details, and human-evaluation sampling and annotation instructions. Prompt documentation is revised, but Figure 6 introduces an inconsistency: the earlier pair of literal reference examples becomes duplicate metaphor inputs while retaining an unrelated response. No new code or data release is documented.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wang et al. (2024b), Wang et al. (2025), and Ye et al. (2026), removes the Spearman reference, and positions the contribution more cautiously as behavioral diagnosis. Most relevant literature remains unchanged. The corrected Wang et al. (2024a) citation is the same Chinese-metaphor work cited in v1.

P1.justification: The title and most existing narrative sections are extensively rewritten, including the abstract, introduction, related work, methods, results, conclusion, and limitations. Terminology shifts from conceptual irrelevance and overlap ratio to semantic attribute alignment and Anchor Score. The numbered appendix is reorganized into Appendices A–H.

P2.justification: V2 revises the framework and geometry diagrams, enlarges and changes the representative plots in Figure 4, replaces Figure 5's doughnut charts with grouped bars, and redesigns prompt panels. The multiple-choice table moves from the appendix to the main text, two terminology tables are consolidated, and appendix plots receive revised axes, legends, and styling while largely retaining their underlying results.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the argument more defensible by withdrawing the uncalibrated error percentage, limiting claims about internal mechanisms and context neglect, and adding anchor checks and independent human validation. The validation remains restricted to 50 extreme cases rated by one annotator. New reporting defects also limit the gain: Figure 5 misidentifies news-only values as full-data results, and Figure 6 introduces an inconsistent prompt example. Overall, evidential calibration improves, but validation and reproducibility remain uneven.
